analysis.title: Kohl's Corp. (KSS): 3Q26 First Take: Comps return to growth + FY26 guidance raised
key_insights: KSS reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $1.76 vs GS/FactSet consensus of $0.00. Comps rose 1.2% vs GS/consensus of -0.5%.

Retail gross margin was 41.0% vs GS/consensus 39.5%, up 145bps Y/Y. About 130bps came from a $45mn tariff refund, the rest from proprietary brands, stronger store sales and BOPIS, partly offset by higher fuel.
Adjusted operating margin was 4.3% vs GS/consensus 1.8%/1.9%. SG&A was 35.1% of sales vs GS/consensus 35.6%/36.4%.
Reported EPS was also helped by a tax benefit worth $1.16 in the quarter, so quality of the beat is lower than the headline.
FY26 GAAP diluted EPS guidance was raised to $4.30-$4.50 from $1.80-$2.40, vs GS/FactSet consensus of $2.13/$2.14.
GS estimates the raise is mostly one-time items: $0.40 real estate gain, $1.17 tax benefit and $1.03 tariff refunds. Underlying guidance improved about $0.35.
FY26 comps and net sales guidance is flat to +0.5% vs -1.5% to flat prior. Operating margin guidance is 4.7%-4.9% vs 3.5%-4.0% prior.
4Q guidance: comps flat to +2% and EPS $0.95-$1.15 including $0.10 of tariff refunds, vs GS/consensus of -0.2%/0.2% comps and $0.94/$0.95 EPS.
Comps were positive in every line of business in 3Q, with sequential improvement. Other revenue of $186mn rose 10.7% Y/Y.
Inventory fell 1.1% Y/Y vs GS expectation of -5.5%. Cash was $723mn vs GS expectation of $774mn.
GS stays Sell with a $15 12-month target based on 3.8x Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA. Stock closed at $21.20, implying 29.2% downside.

market_movers.rationale: GS sees an encouraging top-line result but most of the guidance raise comes from tariff refunds, real estate gains and a tax benefit. Sell and $15 target are kept.

earnings_insights: KSS 3Q26 adjusted EPS $1.76 reported (recurring) vs GS/FactSet consensus est $0.00. GAAP EPS $2.15 reported, including $0.40 one-time items and a $1.16 tax benefit.
3Q26 total revenue $3.638bn reported, +1.8% Y/Y, vs GS/consensus est $3.558bn/$3.544bn.
3Q26 comps +1.2% reported vs GS/consensus est -0.5%. Adjusted operating margin 4.3% reported vs GS/consensus est 1.8%/1.9%.
FY26 guidance raised: GAAP diluted EPS $4.30-$4.50 vs prior $1.80-$2.40 and GS/FactSet consensus est $2.13/$2.14. Includes $0.40 real estate gain, $1.17 tax benefit and $1.03 tariff refunds.
4Q26 guidance: EPS $0.95-$1.15 including $0.10 tariff refunds, vs GS/consensus est $0.94/$0.95. Comps flat to +2% vs GS/consensus est -0.2%/0.2%.
GS FY1/27E EPS estimate is $2.13 (pre-print) and 4Q (1/27E quarter) EPS estimate is $0.94.
risk_factors: Upside risks to the Sell: top-line reacceleration, cleaner inventories enabling margin recapture, better Sephora shop-in-shop uplift, and an improving wage environment.
Guidance quality is low because most of the raise is one-time.
Higher fuel costs weighed on gross margin.
Sustaining early holiday momentum into 2027 is uncertain.
geopolitical: Tariff refunds are a material benefit to KSS gross margin and guidance, worth $45mn in 3Q and $1.03 per share in the FY26 outlook.

key_data_points.anchor: KSS reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $1.76, above GS/FactSet consensus of $0.00.
Retail gross profit margin was above expectations at 41.0% vs. GS/consensus at 39.5%.
The company now expects 2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $4.30-$4.50 vs. $1.80-$2.40 prior

key_data_points.metric: tariff refund benefit in 3Q gross margin
key_data_points.anchor: reported results included a $45mn tariff refund benefit that flowed through gross margin
Our $15, 12-month price target is based on 3.8x Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA.
EPS in the range of $0.95-$1.15 (inclusive of $0.10 of tariff refunds)
KSS quarter-end inventory decreased 1.1% Y/Y vs. GS expectations for a -5.5% change.

tension_points.bull_case: Comps returned to growth, positive in every line of business, with underlying guidance up about $0.35 and 4Q comps guided flat to +2%.
tension_points.bear_case: Most of the FY26 EPS raise reflects one-time tariff refunds, a real estate gain and a tax benefit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure to sustain early holiday momentum into 2027 would undercut the improving top-line view.

theme_stances.key_argument: The majority of the guidance raise comes from one-time adjustments, though underlying guidance improved about $0.35.
theme_stances.evidence: the majority of the guidance raise is a result of these one-time adjustments
